Buddhist Vegetarian Stir-Fry

Served at: Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 15 min

This Buddhist Vegetarian Stir-Fry is a flavorful and wholesome dish commonly prepared during the Ullambana or Ghost Festival, a time when offerings are made to honor ancestors and spirits. The dish is entirely plant-based, reflecting the Buddhist principle of non-harm and compassion towards all living beings.

Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 inch piece ginger, minced
  • 1 cup sliced shiitake mushrooms (about 70 g)
  • 1 cup broccoli florets (about 90 g)
  • 1 cup sliced carrots (about 120 g)
  • 1 cup snap peas (about 80 g)
  • 1 block firm tofu, drained and cubed (14 oz / 400 g)
  • 3 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon hoisin sauce
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1/4 cup vegetable broth or water (60 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon water
  • 2 green onions, sliced
  • 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds

Method

  1. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
  2. Add minced garlic and ginger; sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
  3. Add tofu cubes and cook until lightly golden on all sides, about 5 minutes.
  4. Add mushrooms, broccoli, carrots, and snap peas; stir-fry for 5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
  5. In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, hoisin sauce, sesame oil, and vegetable broth.
  6. Pour the sauce mixture over the vegetables and tofu; stir well to combine.
  7. Add the cornstarch slurry and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
  8. Remove from heat and garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds before serving.

Tips

  • Use seasonal vegetables available locally to honor the spirit of the festival.
  • For extra protein, add cooked edamame or tempeh.
  • Serve with steamed jasmine rice or noodles for a complete meal.
